proposal: The Mandate says the next Administration should extend the African Growth and Opportunity Act, which gives eligible African countries duty-free access to US markets, beyond its 2025 expiration, but within a strategic framework that rewards good governance and pro-market economic policies rather than channeling benefits to governments that fail to reform.

status_summary: AGOA's prior authorization expired on 2025-09-30. Public Law 119-75 (Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2026, enacted 2026-02-03) reauthorized it through 2026-12-31, with liquidation or reliquidation on request for covered entries made after 2025-09-30 and before enactment, and Proclamation 11030 (signed 2026-05-19) implemented the extension and designated Gabon as a beneficiary effective 2026-01-01. Public Law 119-103 (H.R. 6500, which passed the House as the AGOA Extension Act 340-54 on 2026-01-12 and the Senate 90-6 on 2026-08-08) became law on 2026-09-02; its Section 2008 moves AGOA dates from 2026 to 2028, and a CITA notice of 2026-09-18 sets apparel limits for 2026-10-01 to 2027-09-30 and describes preferential treatment as running through 2028-12-31. USTR requested comments on modernizing AGOA on 2026-04-29 and began the 2027 country eligibility review on 2026-06-30, but no legislation changing eligibility, graduation or reciprocity criteria and no 2027 eligibility determinations were found as of 2026-10-21, so the extension is in law while the strategic-framework element remains at the recommendation stage.

timeline.event: AGOA's prior authorization expires, according to USTR's later notice.

The House passes H.R. 6500, introduced on 2025-12-09 as a bill to extend AGOA (passed under the title AGOA Extension Act, reported by Ways and Means on 2025-12-30), 340-54 (Roll no. 14) under suspension of the rules; the bill later became the vehicle for Public Law 119-103.

Public Law 119-75 (Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2026, H.R. 7148) is enacted; the GovInfo public law page dates it 2026-02-03. USTR's 2026-04-29 notice (below) describes it as reauthorizing AGOA through 2026-12-31, retroactive to 2025-09-30.

Section 5019 (Division I) of Public Law 119-75 amends 19 U.S.C. 2466b to substitute 2026-12-31 for 2025-09-30 as the end date (140 Stat. 632); a retroactive application note provides that covered entries made after 2025-09-30 and before enactment are liquidated or reliquidated on a request filed with CBP within 180 days of enactment, with amounts paid without interest within 90 days.
timeline.source: Legal Information Institute, Cornell Law School (U.S. Code reproduction)

timeline.event: USTR publishes a request for comments on modernizing AGOA to inform recommendations to Congress, covering eligibility criteria, graduation, reciprocity, critical minerals supply chains and enforcement; comments closed 2026-05-15 with 136 received.

Proclamation 11030 (published 2026-05-22) implements the AGOA extension through 2026-12-31, including the regional apparel and third-country fabric programs, and designates Gabon as a beneficiary effective 2026-01-01.

USTR opens its annual review of country eligibility for AGOA for calendar year 2027, conditioned on reauthorization, applying criteria that include a market-based economy, rule of law, anti-corruption systems and worker rights, with a public hearing on 2026-07-23.
The Senate passes H.R. 6500 with an amendment and an amendment to the title, 90-6 (Record Vote 228).
The House agrees to the Senate amendments to H.R. 6500, 370-48 (Roll no. 286) under suspension of the rules; the bill is presented and signed on 2026-09-02 as Public Law 119-103.

Public Law 119-103 (Continuing Appropriations and Extensions Act, 2027) is enacted; its Section 2008 changes the 2026 dates in AGOA's termination provision, regional apparel program and third-country fabric program to 2028 and sets the apparel program's end at 2028-12-31. The text states no new eligibility conditions.

The Committee for the Implementation of Textile Agreements publishes a notice (91 FR 59114), effective 2026-10-01, setting the AGOA duty-free apparel import limit at 1,690,799,016 square meter equivalents (845,399,508 for the lesser-developed country rule) for 2026-10-01 through 2027-09-30, citing Section 5019 of Division I of Public Law 119-75 and Section 2008 of Division B of Public Law 119-103, and stating the latter extends preferential treatment through 2028-12-31.

title: Extend AGOA past 2025 within a framework that rewards good governance
uncertainties: The govinfo.gov copy of Public Law 119-75 (HTML and PDF) ends within Division A (sections 8044 to 8072), so Division I, section 5019 was not read in the enrolled text; it is read through the Code page described next, and USTR's 2026-04-29 notice. The amendment notes on the law.cornell.edu U.S. Code page for 19 U.S.C. 2466b (read 2026-10-22) cite section 5019(a)(1)(A) (Division I) of Public Law 119-75 (2026-02-03, 140 Stat. 632), which substitutes the end date 2026-12-31 for 2025-09-30, and a retroactive application note under section 5019(a)(2): covered entries made after 2025-09-30 and before enactment are liquidated or reliquidated on a request filed with CBP within 180 days of enactment, with amounts paid without interest within 90 days; so the retroactivity is a refund route on request. An external retrieval of the enrolled text additionally reports that section 5019 extends the regional apparel and third-country fabric programs to 2026-12-31 and adds no eligibility conditions (not verified against an opened copy). Section 2008 of Division B of Public Law 119-103 was opened on govinfo.gov on 2026-10-22 (approved 2026-09-02; the page headers place the Act at 140 Stat. 987 and the section at 140 Stat. 1001), through the fetch's extracted text rather than a raw page: it replaces 2026 with 2028 in 19 U.S.C. 2466b and in 19 U.S.C. 3721(g), replaces the regional apparel program's 23 succeeding one-year periods with each succeeding one-year period until 2028-12-31 and changes 2026 to 2028 in its clause (ii)(II), changes 2026 to 2028 in the third-country fabric provisions, and contains no effective-date clause, no new eligibility condition and no retroactive paragraph. The end date of the main provisions is therefore 2028 in the text; that it is 2028-12-31 is an inference from the 2026-12-31 date in the section 5019 amendment note with the year replaced, supported by the CITA notice of 2026-09-18, which describes preferential treatment as running through 2028-12-31. The eligibility-review notice has an internal conflict on the testimony deadline (2026-07-09 versus 2026-07-13). Congress's role in modernizing AGOA and any pending reform bill were not searched. The Mandate does not define the strategic framework, so the match between existing eligibility criteria and the Mandate's good-governance condition is a judgment. Freshness check on 2026-10-21: GovInfo BILLSTATUS for H.R. 6500 confirms the vehicle, vote counts and enactment of Public Law 119-103 on 2026-09-02, and the 2026-09-18 CITA notice cites Section 2008 of Division B of that law and Section 5019 (Division I) of Public Law 119-75 and describes preferential treatment as running through 2028-12-31. USTR's eligible-country page showed no 2027 list, and no reform bill or enacted change to the eligibility criteria was located in a web search. The law.cornell.edu page for 19 U.S.C. 2466b does not yet reflect Public Law 119-103.
